title: Conditional Execution
learning_outcomes: Explain the key behavior of conditional execution and identify when it should be used.
Configure or review the workflow fields and permissions relevant to conditional execution.
Verify the result using a controlled run or static check and interpret the evidence.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on conditional execution. The `if` key conditionally runs steps or jobs; status-check functions and skipped dependencies affect whether later work executes. Use the example to predict the workflow result, then verify the behavior in a safe test repository or by static review.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The `if` key conditionally runs steps or jobs; status-check functions and skipped dependencies affect whether later work executes. Contexts, environment variables, and expressions have different scopes and evaluation times. Treat event data as untrusted and avoid interpolating untrusted values directly into shell source. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.text: Match the event to the intended lifecycle, then test positive and negative branch/path/activity cases. Event payloads may be attacker-controlled, and scheduled jobs use UTC rather than a guaranteed exact start time.

items.text: Use filters to reduce unnecessary runs only when skipped work is genuinely unrelated. Include shared dependencies and test the changed and unchanged path cases so required checks are not bypassed.

content_blocks.code:
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Validate input and exit status"
  report:
    needs: validate
    if: ${{ always() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Inspect the dependency result before acting"
content_blocks.expected_output: The reporting job waits for the validation job and runs even after it finishes; real cleanup/reporting logic should inspect `needs.validate.result` before making decisions.

content_blocks.title: Practice and verification
content_blocks.text: Inspect the example and make one focused change related to conditional execution. Predict the expected result first, then use the run instructions or a static review to check it. items.title: Evidence
items.text: Use the run summary and first failing step. A green result is meaningful only when the intended checks actually ran.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain conditional execution, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Pass explicit values between workflow components while treating event data as untrusted input.

content.task: Apply conditional execution to a small workflow change. State the expected result first, validate the configuration, then record evidence from the run or static check.
task_acceptance_criteria: Identify the relevant event, workflow field, runner behavior, or security boundary.
Explain the expected success result and at least one failure or skip condition.
Use least privilege and a disposable/test context; do not include credentials or production resources.
hints: Start with the key behavior: The `if` key conditionally runs steps or jobs; status-check functions and skipped dependencies affect whether later work executes.
Inspect the exact event filters, permissions, expressions, inputs, and job dependencies that affect this example.

content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: The `if` key conditionally runs steps or jobs; status-check functions and skipped dependencies affect whether later work executes. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
summary: The `if` key conditionally runs steps or jobs; status-check functions and skipped dependencies affect whether later work executes.
Contexts, environment variables, and expressions have different scopes and evaluation times. Treat event data as untrusted and avoid interpolating untrusted values directly into shell source.
Use the provided example as a starting point, replace placeholders with repository-specific checks, and validate both success and expected failure behavior before publication.
